Secret Service Agent Robert Wanko wields an Uzi machine gun, which he had pulled from his briefcase, moments after the attempted assassination of President Reagan. Washington, D.C. March 30, 1981.

Here is a photo series of the event. In the last picture you can see Wanko's empty briefcase lying on the ground.

At 2:27 p.m., Reagan exited a speaking engagement at the Washington Hilton Hotel, towards his waiting limousine, Shooter John Hinckley Jr. waited within a crowd of admirers. As Reagan passed right in front of Hinckley, he fired a Röhm RG-14 .22 revolver six times in 1.7 seconds, missing the president with all but one shot.

The 1st bullet hit White House Press Secretary James Brady in the head. The 2nd hit D.C. police officer Thomas Delahanty in the back of his neck. The 3rd overshot Reagan and hit the window of a building across the street. As Special Agent In Charge Jerry Parr quickly pushed Reagan into the limousine, the 4th hit Secret Service agent Timothy McCarthy in the abdomen as he spread his body over Reagan to make himself a target. The 5th hit the bullet-resistant glass of the window of the limousine. The 6th and final bullet ricocheted off the armored limousine and hit the president in his left underarm, grazing a rib and lodging in his lung causing it to partially collapse, and stopped nearly 1 inch (25mm) from his heart.

After the shooting, Alfred Antenucci, a Cleveland, Ohio, labor official who was standing near Hinckley, was the first to respond. He hit Hinckley in the head and pulled him to the ground. Then Agent Dennis McCarthy dove onto Hinckley. Agent Robert Wanko took an Uzi from a briefcase to cover the President's evacuation and to deter a potential group attack.

Reagan suffered a punctured lung and heavy internal bleeding, but prompt medical attention allowed him to recover quickly. Press Secretary James Brady, who was left paralyzed from a gunshot wound, died in 2014 of causes a Virginia medical examiner found were directly related to the 1981 shooting.

Hinckley, who claimed that he did it in an effort to impress actress Jodie Foster, was found not guilty by reason of insanity on charges of attempting to assassinate the President and remains confined to a psychiatric facility.
